title: Expressive writing can help your mental health, with James Pennebaker, PhD

sentences.en: Have you ever kept a diary?
sentences.zh: 你写过日记吗？

sentences.en: For many people, journaling is a lifetime habit.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，写日记是一种终身的习惯。

sentences.en: Others may turn to it in moments of stress or during major life transitions.
sentences.zh: 其他人可能在压力时刻或人生重大转折期间才会动笔。

sentences.en: But in fact, psychologists' research suggests that we all might want to consider occasionally writing about our lives, even those of us who don't consider ourselves writers.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，心理学家的研究表明，我们所有人都应该考虑偶尔写写自己的生活，即使是我们中那些并不认为自己是作家的人。

sentences.en: That's because researchers have found that expressive writing can improve people's mental and even their physical health and can help us work through challenges in our lives.
sentences.zh: 这是因为研究人员发现，表达性写作可以改善人们的心理甚至生理健康，并能帮助我们解决生活中的挑战。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about why that is.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨其中的原因。

sentences.en: We're also going to talk about the power of words more generally and about how the words we use can offer insights into our emotions, motivations, and personality.
sentences.zh: 我们还将更广泛地讨论文字的力量，以及我们使用的词汇如何提供对情绪、动机和个性的洞察。

sentences.en: So why does writing about our lives improve our mental health?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么写下我们的生活能改善心理健康呢？

sentences.en: Do you have to write every day to see these effects?
sentences.zh: 你必须每天写才能看到这些效果吗？

sentences.en: Does it matter how a person writes?
sentences.zh: 一个人的写作方式重要吗？

sentences.en: Are there guidelines to follow if you want to try it?
sentences.zh: 如果你想尝试，有什么准则需要遵循吗？

sentences.en: And how does language connect to emotions, motivations, and personality?
sentences.zh: 语言又是如何与情绪、动机和个性联系起来的？

sentences.en: What do the words we use tell us about ourselves and each other?
sentences.zh: 我们使用的词汇向我们揭示了关于自己和彼此的什么信息？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. James Pennebaker, a professor emeritus of psychology at the University of Texas at Austin.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是得克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的心理学荣誉退休教授詹姆斯·彭尼贝克博士。

sentences.en: He conducted pioneering research on expressive writing in the 1980s and 90s.
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪80年代和90年代对表达性写作进行了开创性的研究。

sentences.en: Since then, he's focused on natural language use and how language, personality, and social behavior interact.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他一直专注于自然语言的使用，以及语言、个性和社会行为如何相互作用。

sentences.en: Dr. Pennebaker is the author or editor of more than 300 articles and 12 books, including
sentences.zh: 彭尼贝克博士是300多篇文章和12本书的作者或编辑，其中包括

sentences.en: Expressive Writing, Words That Heal, and The Secret Life of Pronouns, What Our Words Say About Us.
sentences.zh: 《表达性写作》、《治愈的文字》以及《代词的秘密生活：我们的文字如何诉说我们自己》。

sentences.en: He has received numerous awards for teaching and research, including the 2016 APA Award for
sentences.zh: 他因教学和研究获得了无数奖项，包括2016年美国心理学会颁发的

sentences.en: Distinguished Applications of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 心理学杰出应用奖。

sentences.en: Dr. Pennebaker, thanks for joining me.
sentences.zh: 彭尼贝克博士，感谢您参加我的节目。

sentences.en: It's great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Let's start with your research on expressive writing.
sentences.zh: 让我们从您关于表达性写作的研究开始谈起。

sentences.en: You're a social psychologist by training, not a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 您受过社会心理学的专业训练，而不是临床心理学家。

sentences.en: So how did you get started studying what eventually became recognized as this powerful therapeutic technique?
sentences.zh: 那么，您是如何开始研究这种最终被公认为强大的治疗技术的呢？

sentences.en: Well, this is actually the story of my life.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这其实就是我的人生故事。

sentences.en: I've never really planned to go in any particular direction, just letting interesting things fall in my lap.
sentences.zh: 我从未真正计划过要朝哪个特定方向发展，只是让有趣的事情自然而然地发生。

sentences.en: Early in my career, I was interested in mind-body issues.
sentences.zh: 在我职业生涯的早期，我对身心问题很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Why do people get sick?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们会生病？

sentences.en: How do you know if you're sick?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道自己生病了？

sentences.en: And I was working on what became an early book called The Psychology of Physical Symptoms,
sentences.zh: 当时我正在撰写后来成为我早期著作之一的《身体症状的心理学》，

sentences.en: and I was thinking, you know, I should do a questionnaire just to get a sense of what kind of people,
sentences.zh: 我在想，你知道，我应该做一份问卷，只是为了了解什么样的人、

sentences.en: what kind of personalities, what kind of life experiences might be related to people reporting physical symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 什么样的性格、什么样的生活经历可能与人们报告的身体症状有关。

sentences.en: And I came up with this giant questionnaire working with students, and we put on questions that things that sounded interesting.
sentences.zh: 于是我与学生们合作设计了一份巨大的问卷，我们在上面添加了一些听起来很有趣的问题。

sentences.en: They didn't have any theoretical basis.
sentences.zh: 它们没有任何理论基础。

sentences.en: We asked about people's diet, how they got along with their parents.
sentences.zh: 我们询问了人们的饮食，以及他们与父母的相处情况。

sentences.en: And one of the students I was working with says, how about this one?
sentences.zh: 我合作的一名学生说，这个怎么样？

sentences.en: Prior to the age of 17, did you ever have a traumatic sexual experience?
sentences.zh: 在17岁之前，你是否有过创伤性的性经历？

sentences.en: And I thought, yeah, that's an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 我想，是的，这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: You know, that's certainly nothing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这当然没什么。

sentences.en: Nobody ever asked that question back in the early 80s.
sentences.zh: 在80年代初，从来没有人问过这个问题。

sentences.en: That one question ended up being one of the most powerful predictor of physical symptoms in health.
sentences.zh: 那个问题最终成为了身体症状和健康状况最强有力的预测指标之一。

sentences.en: And I later did this with a national sample.
sentences.zh: 后来我用全国样本做了同样的调查。

sentences.en: And again, people who endorsed that items were more likely to have been hospitalized for any cause in the previous years.
sentences.zh: 结果再次显示，那些认可该选项的人在过去几年中因各种原因住院的可能性更高。

sentences.en: It was related to colds, flus, cancer, high blood pressure, you name it.
sentences.zh: 它与感冒、流感、癌症、高血压等各种疾病有关。

sentences.en: And I became fascinated.
sentences.zh: 我开始着迷了。

sentences.en: What is it about a traumatic sexual experience?
sentences.zh: 创伤性性经历到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And as I started to do more studies, I discovered it wasn't just a traumatic sexual experience.
sentences.zh: 随着我开始做更多的研究，我发现这不仅仅是创伤性性经历的问题。

sentences.en: It was having any kind of traumatic experience that people kept secret.
sentences.zh: 而是任何人们保守秘密的创伤性经历。

sentences.en: Now, we had known for forever that traumas were bad for physical health.
sentences.zh: 我们早就知道创伤对身体健康有害。

sentences.en: That wasn't news.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么新闻。

sentences.en: But having a trauma of any kind and keeping it secret really increased the toxicity of that trauma.
sentences.zh: 但经历任何形式的创伤并将其保密，确实增加了这种创伤的毒性。

sentences.en: In other words, secrets in and of themselves were toxic.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，秘密本身就是有毒的。

sentences.en: And this made me wonder, if secrets are so bad, what if we brought people in the laboratory and had them talk about them?
sentences.zh: 这让我想到，如果秘密这么糟糕，如果我们把人们带到实验室让他们谈论这些秘密会怎样？

sentences.en: Or that turned out to be way too complex.
sentences.zh: 结果发现那太复杂了。

sentences.en: How about we just had them write about it?
sentences.zh: 如果我们只是让他们写下来呢？

sentences.en: And that was kind of the birth of expressive writing.
sentences.zh: 这算是表达性写作的诞生。

sentences.en: So what is it about expressive writing that helps people?
sentences.zh: 那么，表达性写作对人们有什么帮助呢？

sentences.en: And how is it different from other types of writing?
sentences.zh: 它与其他类型的写作有何不同？

sentences.en: For example, just writing letters, essays, or even lists that we write to keep ourselves organized.
sentences.zh: 例如，仅仅是写信、写文章，甚至是为保持条理而写的清单。

sentences.en: We'll get into those questions because those questions are actually much deeper than you might expect.
sentences.zh: 我们会深入探讨这些问题，因为这些问题实际上比你想象的要深刻得多。

sentences.en: The quick answer is there in many of these approaches probably are just about as effective.
sentences.zh: 简单的回答是，其中许多方法可能同样有效。

sentences.en: What I did with that first study, I had no idea of should I have people write once or how many times should I have them write?
sentences.zh: 在最初的那项研究中，我根本不知道是应该让人写一次，还是应该让他们写多少次？

sentences.en: And the first studies were all done with college students.
sentences.zh: 最初的研究都是以大学生为对象进行的。

sentences.en: I decided it would make sense to have people write maybe three or four times.
sentences.zh: 我决定让人写三四次是有意义的。

sentences.en: And I needed to do an experiment in an efficient way.
sentences.zh: 而且我需要以一种有效的方式进行实验。

sentences.en: And so I would have people, they were randomly assigned by a flip of the coin to either write about a traumatic experience for four days or about superficial topics for four days.
sentences.zh: 所以我让人们通过掷硬币的方式被随机分配，要么连续四天写创伤经历，要么连续四天写肤浅的话题。

sentences.en: And I needed to have them write it in a laboratory at the university.
sentences.zh: 我需要让他们在大学的实验室里写。

sentences.en: And this study was done at Southern Methodist University in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 这项研究是在达拉斯的南卫理公会大学进行的。

sentences.en: And I needed enough rooms and I wanted to line everybody up essentially and essentially have
sentences.zh: 我需要足够的房间，我想把每个人基本上排成一队，让

sentences.en: somebody come in at four in the afternoon, 410, 420, et cetera, and just line them up and run all 50 or so people in an afternoon.
sentences.zh: 某人在下午四点、四点十分、四点二十分等时间进来，把他们排好，在一个下午内完成所有50人左右的实验。

sentences.en: And to do that, I needed a lot of rooms and I was able to get enough rooms to run for four hours.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，我需要很多房间，我设法弄到了足够的房间来运行四个小时。

sentences.en: And I had a lot of people helping me and we could only get those rooms for a week, which was really four days, Monday through Thursday.
sentences.zh: 我有很多帮手，我们只能租用这些房间一周，实际上是四天，从周一到周四。

sentences.en: And just doing the arithmetic, that meant that everyone could write in that first study, I believe it was 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 简单算一下，这意味着在第一项研究中，每个人都可以写，我相信是15分钟。

sentences.en: And they wrote for four days because that's all we could get to, get the times.
sentences.zh: 他们写了四天，因为我们只能争取到这么多时间。

sentences.en: And it had to be after all classes had finished.
sentences.zh: 而且必须在所有课程结束后进行。

sentences.en: And so it were all these practical considerations.
sentences.zh: 所以这都是出于实际考虑。

sentences.en: And that first study was powerful because those people who were asked to write about upsetting
sentences.zh: 第一项研究很有影响力，因为那些被要求写下令人不安的

sentences.en: experiences ended up going to the student health center at about half the rates of people in our controls.
sentences.zh: 经历的人，去学生健康中心的频率大约只有对照组的一半。

sentences.en: So there was no great theory of how much they should write.
sentences.zh: 所以关于他们应该写多少，并没有什么伟大的理论。

sentences.en: There was no great foresight in terms of what they should write about.
sentences.zh: 在他们应该写什么方面，也没有什么远见卓识。

sentences.en: And that was the other issue.
sentences.zh: 那是另一个问题。

sentences.en: What should I have them write about?
sentences.zh: 我应该让他们写什么？

sentences.en: Well, I didn't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: So I thought, you know, I'll have them write about a really traumatic experience that they've had.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，我会让他们写下他们经历过的真正创伤性的经历。

sentences.en: And actually, here were the first instructions that I gave.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是我给出的第一批指令。

sentences.en: For the next four days, what I'd like to have you do is to really let go and explore your deepest thoughts and feelings about the most upsetting or traumatic experience of your
sentences.zh: 在接下来的四天里，我希望你们真正放下包袱，探索关于你们一生中最令人不安或创伤性的经历的

sentences.en: entire life.
sentences.zh: 最深层的想法和感受。

sentences.en: I really want you to let go.
sentences.zh: 我真的希望你们能释放出来。

sentences.en: And as you write, I want you to write continuously.
sentences.zh: 在写作时，我希望你们持续地写。

sentences.en: Don't worry about spelling or grammar or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 不要担心拼写、语法或类似的事情。

sentences.en: And in your writing, you might write about how it relates to other issues in your life, maybe related to your childhood, maybe related to school, or how it can be related to your
sentences.zh: 在写作中，你们可以写它如何与生活中的其他问题相关联，也许与童年有关，也许与学校有关，或者它如何与你们的

sentences.en: friendships, or who you'd like to be in the future, or who you've been in the past, or who you are now.
sentences.zh: 友谊相关联，或者你们未来想成为什么样的人，或者你们过去是什么样的人，或者你们现在是什么样的人。

sentences.en: And you can write about the same traumatic experience all four days, or you can write something different each day.
sentences.zh: 你们可以四天都写同一个创伤经历，也可以每天写不同的内容。

sentences.en: That's entirely up to you.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于你们自己。

sentences.en: And in fact, many people have never had a trauma, but all of us have had major stressors or conflicts.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多人从未经历过创伤，但我们所有人都经历过重大的压力或冲突。

sentences.en: And you can write about those as well.
sentences.zh: 你们也可以写这些内容。

sentences.en: And ideally, I'd like to have you focus on something that you haven't talked to other people about much.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，我希望你们专注于一些你们没有怎么跟别人谈论过的事情。

sentences.en: So for the next four days, I really want you to really let go and write.
sentences.zh: 所以接下来的四天，我真的希望你们能真正放下包袱，写出来。

sentences.en: So that was the instruction.
sentences.zh: 这就是指令。

sentences.en: And then people who were assigned to the control condition were asked to write about superficial topics.
sentences.zh: 然后，被分配到对照组的人被要求写一些肤浅的话题。

sentences.en: Initially, we had them write about things like the shoes they were wearing or their dorm room or something like that.
sentences.zh: 最初，我们让他们写一些诸如他们穿的鞋子、宿舍房间之类的事情。

sentences.en: But then later, I became fascinated with time management.
sentences.zh: 但后来，我对时间管理产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: I've always been dismissive of time management.
sentences.zh: 我一直对时间管理不屑一顾。

sentences.en: You know, to me, I think that's kind of training for obsessive compulsive disorder.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对我来说，我认为那有点像是强迫症的训练。

sentences.en: In any case, what I did was after the first couple of studies, I would, in the control condition, I'd ask people how they use their time.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我所做的是在最初的几项研究之后，在对照组中，我会问人们如何利用他们的时间。

sentences.en: What did you do during the last 24 hours?
sentences.zh: 过去24小时你做了什么？

sentences.en: What do you plan to do during the next 24 hours?
sentences.zh: 你计划在接下来的24小时内做什么？

sentences.en: What did you do last week, et cetera?
sentences.zh: 上周你做了什么，等等？

sentences.en: And having them focus on details.
sentences.zh: 让他们专注于细节。

sentences.en: And I'm pleased to say that never was associated with any improvements in health or anything else.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地说，这从来没有与健康或其他方面的任何改善联系在一起。

sentences.en: So, but everybody thought it was, you know, they thought that, well, it's time management.
sentences.zh: 所以，每个人都认为，你知道，他们认为，嗯，这是时间管理。

sentences.en: It must be good.
sentences.zh: 它一定很好。

sentences.en: But the point with this was in those first studies, we were focusing on traumas.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，在最初的那些研究中，我们专注于创伤。

sentences.en: And then I started having people write about different topics.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始让人写不同的主题。

sentences.en: One of my next studies was having people not writing about the most traumatic experience of their lives.
sentences.zh: 我的下一项研究之一是让人不写他们一生中最创伤性的经历。

sentences.en: But I got college freshmen who were just starting college, and I would have them write about
sentences.zh: 我找了刚上大学的大一新生，让他们写下

sentences.en: their deepest thoughts and feelings about coming to college with the same general instructions, tie this into other experiences.
sentences.zh: 他们关于上大学的最深层想法和感受，并给出相同的通用指令，将此与其他经历联系起来。

sentences.en: And we got the same effects.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了同样的效果。

sentences.en: And then we started doing more and more studies with people who got laid off from their jobs or you name it.
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始对那些被解雇的人等等进行越来越多的研究。

sentences.en: It seemed in those first few years, we started doing more and more studies, having people write about anything.
sentences.zh: 在最初的几年里，我们似乎开始做越来越多的研究，让人写任何东西。

sentences.en: And those first studies, we had them write for four.
sentences.zh: 在最初的那些研究中，我们让他们写了四天。

sentences.en: The first one, I think it was four days, 15 minutes a day.
sentences.zh: 第一次，我想是四天，每天15分钟。

sentences.en: The second study, I think, was 20 minutes a day for four days.
sentences.zh: 第二次研究，我想是每天20分钟，持续四天。

sentences.en: And then their next study was three days.
sentences.zh: 然后接下来的研究是三天。

sentences.en: And then that study after that was five days.
sentences.zh: 再之后的研究是五天。

sentences.en: And sometimes it would be as little as 10 minutes, sometimes as long as 30 minutes.
sentences.zh: 有时短至10分钟，有时长至30分钟。

sentences.en: And they all got similar effects.
sentences.zh: 它们都得到了类似的效果。

sentences.en: So that ended up being kind of the basis of this.
sentences.zh: 所以这最终成为了这项研究的基础。

sentences.en: And it's ironic that there have now been over 2,000 studies published on expressive writing.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，现在已经有超过2000项关于表达性写作的研究发表了。

sentences.en: I'm astounded by this.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到震惊。

sentences.en: I can't even keep up with the literature.
sentences.zh: 我甚至跟不上文献的更新速度。

sentences.en: I was recently looking online with Google Scholar how many papers have been published on expressive writing in the last year.
sentences.zh: 我最近在谷歌学术上查看去年发表了多少关于表达性写作的论文。

sentences.en: And it's about 200.
sentences.zh: 大约有200篇。

sentences.en: It's really quite surprising.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And some of the studies work.
sentences.zh: 有些研究有效。

sentences.en: Some of them don't work.
sentences.zh: 有些则无效。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not a giant effect.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不是一个巨大的效应。

sentences.en: But what's been interesting is some people will have individuals write for two days, three days, four days, five days.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，有些人会让个人写两天、三天、四天、五天。

sentences.en: Some will have them write once a week for four weeks.
sentences.zh: 有些人会让他们每周写一次，持续四周。

sentences.en: Sometimes they'll have them write several times in one day.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会让他们在一天内写几次。

sentences.en: Sometimes they'll have them write 20 minutes, 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会让他们写20分钟、10分钟。

sentences.en: There's even been a couple of studies where people write just two minutes each time.
sentences.zh: 甚至有几项研究是人们每次只写两分钟。

sentences.en: And again, they all seem to work.
sentences.zh: 同样，它们似乎都有效。

sentences.en: Is there a greater effect for the deeper feelings?
sentences.zh: 对于更深层的感受，效果会更大吗？

sentences.en: Is that what you're seeing?
sentences.zh: 这就是你所看到的吗？

sentences.en: So in addition to secret, it's something that is really heartfelt and deep inside?
sentences.zh: 除了秘密之外，它是否也是一种发自内心、深藏于心底的东西？

sentences.en: I think the heartfelt deep inside is true with all of these.
sentences.zh: 我认为“发自内心、深藏于心底”这一点适用于所有这些情况。

sentences.en: And even if you write for two minutes, what's interesting is there's a false sense that, oh, you're only writing for two minutes, four times.
sentences.zh: 即使你只写两分钟，有趣的是，人们会产生一种错觉，觉得“哦，你只是分四次，每次写了两分钟而已”。

sentences.en: That's only eight minutes.
sentences.zh: 那总共才八分钟。

sentences.en: It can't possibly work.
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能有效呢？

sentences.en: Well, the reality is you're writing for those two minutes, but you're thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实是，你确实只写了那两分钟，但你一直在思考它。

sentences.en: You leave the lab and you start pondering it, and you might talk to somebody about it.
sentences.zh: 你离开实验室后会开始琢磨这件事，甚至可能会找人谈论它。

sentences.en: You live with that experience over the course of the study.
sentences.zh: 在整个研究过程中，你都在与那种体验共处。

sentences.en: And so look how most people are, and I'm one of these most peoples.
sentences.zh: 看看大多数人是怎么做的吧，我也是其中之一。

sentences.en: You know, I never was a dedicated writer, and I'm still not a dedicated writer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我从来都不是一个勤奋的写作者，现在也不是。

sentences.en: I write when I need to.
sentences.zh: 我只在需要的时候才写。

sentences.en: And it used to be if I was upset about something, I had a fight with my wife or there'd been conflict at work or whatever,
sentences.zh: 过去，如果我对某事感到心烦，比如和妻子吵架了，或者工作中出现了冲突之类的，

sentences.en: what I would do is I would not talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我会选择闭口不谈。

sentences.en: You know, I'd walk down the street, and I'd start thinking about it, and then I said, oh, I should have said this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我会走在街上，开始思考这件事，然后对自己说：“哦，我当时应该这么说。”

sentences.en: And then I'll think about something else.
sentences.zh: 然后我会去想别的事情。

sentences.en: And then I think, oh, I should write about this.
sentences.zh: 接着我又想：“哦，我应该把这些写下来。”

sentences.en: No, it'll just make me think about it too much, which, of course, is stupid, because I'm already thinking about it too much.
sentences.zh: 不，那只会让我对它想得太多。当然，这很愚蠢，因为我本来就已经想得太多了。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 确实，确实。

sentences.en: And so getting people to actually sit down and confront it and to write it, you don't have to write a lot, but you have to,
sentences.zh: 所以，让人们真正坐下来面对并写下这些事情——你不必写很多，但你必须，

sentences.en: first of all, just acknowledge it and put it into words.
sentences.zh: 首先，仅仅是承认它并将其诉诸文字。

sentences.en: And that was really, for me, the breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这确实是一个突破。

sentences.en: Do people have to write on a regular basis to see a really significant effect?
sentences.zh: 人们是否需要定期写作才能看到显著的效果？

sentences.en: Like, do I have to write something every day to really experience the benefits?
sentences.zh: 比如，我是否必须每天写点什么才能真正体验到好处？

sentences.en: Oh, my God, no.
sentences.zh: 天哪，完全不用。

sentences.en: To give you an example, I write maybe two or three times a year.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我一年大概只写两三次。

sentences.en: You know, when something miserable is going on, you know, when I hear about journaling and writing every day, I just get nervous about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当生活陷入困境时，听到关于每天写日记的建议，我反而会感到紧张。

sentences.en: I would hate that because I use writing when I'm dealing with something that is ugly, unpleasant, painful.
sentences.zh: 我会很讨厌那样，因为我只在处理丑陋、令人不快或痛苦的事情时才会写作。

sentences.en: And if life is going well, why in the world do I want to introspect it?
sentences.zh: 如果生活一切顺利，我为什么要没事找事去进行内省呢？

sentences.en: You know, I want to enjoy life when it's here, and when there's bad things, writing for me helps me get through them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当生活美好时，我想享受它；而当坏事发生时，写作能帮我度过难关。

sentences.en: And so I view it almost as, I've often thought of it as an antibiotic.
sentences.zh: 所以我几乎把它看作——我常把它比作抗生素。

sentences.en: You know, you have all these bad things going on, and then you use this method to get past it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你遇到各种糟糕的事情时，就用这种方法来克服它。

sentences.en: And then next time something bad happens, I'll use writing again.
sentences.zh: 下次再有坏事发生，我还会再用写作。

sentences.en: Is there a difference between writing something by hand or writing on a computer, or what about talking to a speech-to-text program?
sentences.zh: 手写和用电脑打字有什么区别吗？或者使用语音转文字软件呢？

sentences.en: Any differences there?
sentences.zh: 这之间有什么差异吗？

sentences.en: There have been now a large number of studies comparing them.
sentences.zh: 现在已经有大量研究对它们进行了比较。

sentences.en: And I'd have to say that on average, there's no difference.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，平均而言，它们之间没有区别。

sentences.en: If you stand back and you squint at the data, you can see a weak effect that writing by hand might work a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 如果你退后一步，仔细审视这些数据，你会发现一个微弱的效应，即手写可能稍微好一点点。

sentences.en: But my colleagues don't really acknowledge the squint test, so it probably doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 但我的同事们并不认可这种“眯眼测试”，所以这可能并不重要。

sentences.en: My recommendation is to do what you're most comfortable with.
sentences.zh: 我的建议是，选择你最舒服的方式去做。

sentences.en: And I've experimented with, and I've actually tested this with people in workshops, having people write using finger writing,
sentences.zh: 我曾做过实验，实际上也在研讨会上测试过，让人们尝试“手指书写”，

sentences.en: where you just, with your finger, write in the air about an upsetting experience.
sentences.zh: 也就是用你的手指在空中写下关于一段痛苦经历的内容。

sentences.en: I invented this years ago when my wife and I were on a vacation somewhere, and we'd had a significant disagreement about something.
sentences.zh: 这是我多年前发明的，当时我和妻子在度假，我们对某件事产生了严重的分歧。

sentences.en: I got up in the middle of the night, and I was thinking, I should write, but if I turn on the lights, it'll wake her up.
sentences.zh: 半夜我醒来，心想我应该写点什么，但如果开灯会把她吵醒。

sentences.en: And so I just sat there and started writing in the air, and I thought, ooh, this works.
sentences.zh: 于是我就坐在那儿开始在空中写，我心想：噢，这招管用。

sentences.en: And it actually does.
sentences.zh: 而且它确实有效。

sentences.en: So I think the real art is translating an emotional experience into words.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为真正的艺术在于将情感体验转化为文字。

sentences.en: And by doing that, that changes the way that experience is organized in the brain, and it slows down your thinking process.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，大脑中组织该体验的方式会发生改变，并减缓你的思维过程。

sentences.en: And it also forces structure in creating a story.
sentences.zh: 它还强迫你在创作故事时建立结构。

sentences.en: In other words, when you're writing, you have to use a complete sentence.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当你写作时，你必须使用完整的句子。

sentences.en: And if you write a complete sentence, your next sentence has to be related to that sentence you just finished.
sentences.zh: 如果你写了一个完整的句子，你的下一个句子必须与你刚刚写完的那个句子相关。

sentences.en: So it's all part of putting together complex emotional topics.
sentences.zh: 所以，这一切都是为了整合复杂的情感话题。

sentences.en: So it sounds like a really great tool.
sentences.zh: 听起来这真是一个很棒的工具。

sentences.en: Would you say it could substitute for therapy, or should you do expressive writing in conjunction with therapy?
sentences.zh: 你会说它可以替代心理治疗吗？还是应该将表达性写作与治疗结合起来使用？

sentences.en: Might that supercharge the effect that you're getting?
sentences.zh: 那样会不会增强你所获得的效果？

sentences.en: So, of course, if I'm talking on an APA podcast and say that this could take the place of therapy, I would be drummed out of the field.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果我在美国心理学会（APA）的播客上说这可以取代心理治疗，我会被赶出这个领域的。

sentences.en: I do think that writing is a powerful method that anybody can use any time, and it's free.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为写作是一种任何人随时都可以使用的强大方法，而且它是免费的。

sentences.en: And if you write a few times and you don't feel as though you're getting any better, I think therapy is a really good alternative, or jogging, or talking to a friend.
sentences.zh: 如果你写了几次却感觉不到任何好转，我认为心理治疗是一个很好的选择，或者去慢跑，或者找朋友倾诉。

sentences.en: I also think writing works wonderfully in conjunction with therapy.
sentences.zh: 我也认为写作与心理治疗结合使用效果极佳。

sentences.en: And I would bet that a very high percentage of therapists actually use some form of writing in conjunction with therapy.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，很大比例的治疗师实际上都在治疗过程中使用了某种形式的写作。

sentences.en: And I've even recommended to therapists to, if they would like to speed up the effectiveness of a therapeutic session, is when the person shows up to meet with you,
sentences.zh: 我甚至向治疗师建议，如果他们想加快治疗过程的效率，当来访者出现时，

sentences.en: and they typically are in the waiting room for five or ten minutes, put them in a room and have them write for five or ten minutes,
sentences.zh: 他们通常会在候诊室待上五到十分钟，让他们在房间里写五到十分钟，

sentences.en: and then bring them into the therapeutic session.
sentences.zh: 然后再带他们进入治疗环节。

sentences.en: And when my friends have tried that, they've been impressed that the people are much more focused on what they want to talk about,
sentences.zh: 当我的朋友尝试这样做时，他们印象深刻，因为人们能更专注于他们想谈论的内容，

sentences.en: they have a better sense of the issues, and it makes therapy go, I think, more efficiently.
sentences.zh: 他们对问题有了更好的感知，我认为这让治疗进行得更有效率。

sentences.en: Let's change gears now and talk for a minute about your more recent work, which is on language analysis, and what we can learn about people from studying their word use.
sentences.zh: 现在换个话题，谈谈你最近关于语言分析的工作，以及通过研究人们的用词我们能了解到什么。

sentences.en: How did you move from expressive writing into this work?
sentences.zh: 你是如何从表达性写作转向这项工作的？

sentences.en: How are they connected, if they are?
sentences.zh: 如果它们之间有联系的话，是如何关联的？

sentences.en: They are intimately connected.
sentences.zh: 它们有着紧密的联系。

sentences.en: You know, I was doing these first studies on expressive writing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时正在做关于表达性写作的初步研究。

sentences.en: We're now into the mid-1990s.
sentences.zh: 时间已经到了90年代中期。

sentences.en: And I was trying to understand who benefited from writing.
sentences.zh: 我当时试图了解谁能从写作中受益。

sentences.en: You know, people didn't always benefit from writing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们并非总能从写作中获益。

sentences.en: And the stories that people were writing were unbelievably powerful.
sentences.zh: 而且人们写下的故事令人难以置信地震撼。

sentences.en: And I was curious, is there some way of writing that may be more effective than others?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，是否有一种写作方式比其他方式更有效？

sentences.en: And so I initially was able to get a large number of graduate students in the counseling program
sentences.zh: 所以我最初设法找了大量的咨询项目研究生，

sentences.en: and have them read these essays and to evaluate them in terms of all these dimensions.
sentences.zh: 让他们阅读这些文章，并从各个维度对它们进行评估。

sentences.en: You know, how self-reflective is this person?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个人有多自我反思？

sentences.en: How effective do you think writing was in changing them?
sentences.zh: 你认为写作在改变他们方面有多有效？

sentences.en: To what degree did they find some kind of meaning?
sentences.zh: 他们在多大程度上找到了一些意义？

sentences.en: How emotional were they?
sentences.zh: 他们的情绪化程度如何？

sentences.en: Et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等。

sentences.en: And what I discovered was that having people, first of all, just read these traumatic stories.
sentences.zh: 我发现，首先，仅仅让人们阅读这些创伤性故事，

sentences.en: And people, by the way, did write really traumatic events that you and I and everybody listened to this,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，人们确实写下了非常创伤性的事件，如果你和我以及每一位听众，

sentences.en: if you read them, you would agree that these were really upsetting experiences.
sentences.zh: 如果你读了它们，你也会同意这些确实是令人心烦的经历。

sentences.en: What we discovered was that people who were reading these stories got depressed reading them because they were so upsetting.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，阅读这些故事的人因为内容太令人难过而变得抑郁。

sentences.en: And also, the judges who were reading them didn't agree on any of the ratings.
sentences.zh: 而且，阅读它们的评审员在任何评分上都无法达成一致。

sentences.en: In other words, here we were essentially having to do mini-therapy with our raters.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们本质上是在对我们的评分员进行小型心理治疗。

sentences.en: And their ratings were not internally consistent or valid.
sentences.zh: 他们的评分既不内部一致，也不具备效度。

sentences.en: And so here was a, oh, and it was really slow and expensive.
sentences.zh: 所以，噢，而且这非常缓慢且昂贵。

sentences.en: This is not a way to build a career if you're trying to understand writing.
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解写作，这不是建立职业生涯的方法。

sentences.en: So I thought, you know, I had taken a little computer science in college.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，你知道，我在大学时学过一点计算机科学。

sentences.en: And I had a sense of how you could write a computer program that could analyze it.
sentences.zh: 我有一种感觉，你可以编写一个计算机程序来分析它。

sentences.en: And by the way, I looked to see if there were any computer programs that existed at the time.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我查了一下当时是否存在任何计算机程序。

sentences.en: And there weren't.
sentences.zh: 结果没有。

sentences.en: I talked to experts all over the country.
sentences.zh: 我咨询了全国各地的专家。

sentences.en: And I told them what I was looking for.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他们我在寻找什么。

sentences.en: And they all agreed it was an interesting project, but they didn't know who could be helpful.
sentences.zh: 他们都同意这是一个有趣的项目，但他们不知道谁能提供帮助。

sentences.en: So I, by the way, I should say, about four years after I had finished writing this computer program with my students,
sentences.zh: 所以，顺便说一下，我应该说，在我与学生们完成这个计算机程序编写大约四年后，

sentences.en: I discovered that there, in fact, had been a really wonderful computer program written by a group out of Harvard in the 1960s, which was, that had preceded me by quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 我发现，事实上，哈佛大学的一个团队在60年代编写了一个非常棒的计算机程序，它比我早得多。

sentences.en: It wouldn't have worked for me at the time because it was built for a giant mainframe computer.
sentences.zh: 它在当时对我来说没用，因为它是为巨型大型机计算机设计的。

sentences.en: But in any case, unfortunately, I had a graduate student in my lab at the time.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，不幸的是，我当时实验室里有一位研究生。

sentences.en: This was about 1992, 93, Martha Francis, whose undergraduate degree had been in computer science.
sentences.zh: 那是大约1992、93年，玛莎·弗朗西斯（Martha Francis），她的本科学位是计算机科学。

sentences.en: And she had taken some years off and had come back to graduate school in social psychology.
sentences.zh: 她休学了几年，又回来攻读社会心理学研究生。

sentences.en: And, you know, I sat with her.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我坐在她身边。

sentences.en: I said, Martha, I've got a great idea for an experiment or for a computer program.
sentences.zh: 我说：“玛莎，我有一个关于实验或计算机程序的绝妙想法。”

sentences.en: And, you know, I think it should be pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为它应该很简单。

sentences.en: I can't believe it'll take more than two or three weeks to write.
sentences.zh: 我不敢相信编写它会超过两三周。

sentences.en: We worked on it.
sentences.zh: 我们开始着手工作。

sentences.en: And that two to three weeks kind of expanded, you know, expanded two or three years.
sentences.zh: 那两三周的时间扩展成了，你知道，扩展成了两三年。

sentences.en: But, you know, such is the nature of science.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，科学的本质就是这样。

sentences.en: And it was it wasn't the program itself that took so long.
sentences.zh: 而且，并不是程序本身花了那么长时间。

sentences.en: It was how do you know, if you're going to tell a computer to look for anger words, you have to tell the computer what are anger words to look for.
sentences.zh: 而是，你知道，如果你要告诉计算机去寻找愤怒的词汇，你必须告诉计算机什么是需要寻找的愤怒词汇。

sentences.en: And so we had to make all of these dictionaries of words.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须制作所有这些词典。

sentences.en: And we started off with the way everybody starts something like this, looking for emotions, you know, anger, happiness, guilt, sadness, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 我们从每个人开始做这类事情的方式入手，寻找情绪，你知道，愤怒、快乐、内疚、悲伤等等。

sentences.en: And then we also wanted some some therapy related words, you know, words like self-reflection, insight, causal thinking, words like because, cause, effect,
sentences.zh: 然后我们还想要一些与治疗相关的词汇，你知道，比如自我反思、洞察力、因果思维，像“因为”、“原因”、“结果”这样的词，

sentences.en: and other dimensions that psychologists were interested in.
sentences.zh: 以及心理学家感兴趣的其他维度。

sentences.en: And then as long as we're at it, we might as well do parts of speech because those don't require a lot of work to figure out.
sentences.zh: 既然都做了，我们不妨也把词性加上，因为弄清楚这些不需要太多工作。

sentences.en: So, you know, articles and prepositions and pronouns and so forth.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，冠词、介词、代词等等。

sentences.en: So that's how we put this computer program together.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们整合这个计算机程序的方式。

sentences.en: It was called, we called it Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count, L-I-W-C.
sentences.zh: 它被称为——我们称之为“语言探究与词汇计数”（Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count），简称LIWC。

sentences.en: And I should say, I had been given a lot of flack because earlier in my career, I'd come up with names of scales that were cute.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，我曾受到很多批评，因为在我职业生涯早期，我起了一些很可爱的量表名称。

sentences.en: And cute was not viewed as science.
sentences.zh: 而“可爱”并不被视为科学。

sentences.en: Not too serious.
sentences.zh: 不够严肃。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count, L-I-W-C.
sentences.zh: “语言探究与词汇计数”，LIWC。

sentences.en: Now that's serious.
sentences.zh: 现在这看起来严肃多了。

sentences.en: But then we, we called the computer program Luke.
sentences.zh: 但后来我们把这个计算机程序命名为“卢克”（Luke）。

sentences.en: So if you ever hear the word Luke, it's either a book of the Bible or it's my computer program.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你听到“Luke”这个词，它要么是《圣经》里的一卷书，要么就是我的计算机程序。

sentences.en: In any case, the Luke program ended up being a marvelous program.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，Luke程序最终成为了一个了不起的程序。

sentences.en: I mean, it's now, it's now in its maybe sixth or seventh edition and the newest version is a real machine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它现在可能已经出到第六或第七版了，最新版本简直是一台真正的机器。

sentences.en: But what it allowed us to do was to go through and go into any expressive writing study and look at the essays people have written.
sentences.zh: 但它允许我们做的是，深入任何表达性写作研究，查看人们写下的文章。

sentences.en: And we started to see that there were certain features that predicted improvement.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到，有一些特定的特征可以预测改善情况。

sentences.en: So if a person, ironically, if a person's writing about a trauma, the more they're able to use positive emotion words, the more likely they are to benefit.
sentences.zh: 所以，讽刺的是，如果一个人在写关于创伤的内容，他们越能使用积极情绪词汇，就越有可能从中受益。

sentences.en: And it's kind of ironic.
sentences.zh: 这有点讽刺。

sentences.en: So if they say they're not happy, nobody cares about them, they don't, they feel no love from anybody.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们说他们不快乐，没人关心他们，他们感觉不到任何人的爱。

sentences.en: Those words, care, loves, things like that are positive emotion words.
sentences.zh: 那些词——关心、爱，诸如此类——都是积极情绪词汇。

sentences.en: So even if they're negating those positive emotion words, they're better off than if they don't use positive emotion words.
sentences.zh: 所以即使他们是在否定这些积极情绪词汇，他们也比那些完全不使用积极情绪词汇的人状况更好。

sentences.en: In other words, if I say I'm not happy, I'm still thinking along that dimension of happiness.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果我说“我不快乐”，我仍然是在快乐这个维度上进行思考。

sentences.en: If I say I'm sad, I'm not thinking about happiness as the alternative.
sentences.zh: 如果我说“我很悲伤”，我就不会把快乐作为替代选项来思考。

sentences.en: So that was one of the first surprising things.
sentences.zh: 所以这是最初令人惊讶的事情之一。

sentences.en: The more powerful effect, however, were cognitive words.
sentences.zh: 然而，更强大的影响是认知词汇。

sentences.en: Early on, we were focusing on a number of types, but one were causal words because cause, effect, reason, rationale.
sentences.zh: 早期，我们关注多种类型，但其中一种是因果词汇，因为原因、结果、理由、基本原理。

sentences.en: And another type were what we called insight words.
sentences.zh: 另一种类型是我们所谓的洞察力词汇。

sentences.en: Understand, realize, know, meaning, words such as that.
sentences.zh: 理解、意识到、知道、意义，诸如此类的词。

sentences.en: And what we discovered was that the more that people use those words over the course of their writing, the more they improve.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，人们在写作过程中使用这些词汇越多，他们的改善就越明显。

sentences.en: That is, the more they were trying to understand what was going on, the more they were trying to construct a story, the more likely they were to benefit.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们越是试图理解正在发生的事情，越是试图构建一个故事，就越有可能从中受益。

sentences.en: Some later studies, we discovered some other issues as well.
sentences.zh: 在后来的一些研究中，我们还发现了其他一些问题。

sentences.en: Pronouns, for example, are really powerful.
sentences.zh: 例如，代词就非常强大。

sentences.en: And, you know, as a social psychologist, I should have picked up on this immediately.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，作为一名社会心理学家，我本应该立刻注意到这一点。

sentences.en: But when I'm using I words, by definition, when I say I'm feeling so-and-so, my use of the word I is a very brief awareness of self.
sentences.zh: 但当我使用“我”（I）这个词时，根据定义，当我说“我感到某某”时，我对“我”这个词的使用是对自我的一种非常短暂的觉知。

sentences.en: So I words are really interesting.
sentences.zh: “我”字的使用确实很有意思。

sentences.en: We know that, actually, people who are depressed start using I words at very high rates.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，实际上，抑郁症患者开始使用“我”字的频率非常高。

sentences.en: And when their depression lifts, I words drop significantly.
sentences.zh: 而当他们的抑郁情绪好转时，“我”字的使用频率会显著下降。

sentences.en: And people who are anxious use more I words.
sentences.zh: 焦虑的人也会更多地使用“我”字。

sentences.en: People who are sad.
sentences.zh: 还有那些感到悲伤的人。

sentences.en: Ironically, we've used this to predict, actually, suicide.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，我们甚至利用这一点来预测自杀倾向。

sentences.en: We've looked at suicidal poets versus non-suicidal poets.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了有自杀倾向的诗人和没有自杀倾向的诗人。

sentences.en: And the two poets don't differ in terms of negative emotion words.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，这两类诗人在负面情绪词的使用上并没有区别。

sentences.en: The big difference is suicidal poets use I words at much higher rates.
sentences.zh: 最大的区别在于，有自杀倾向的诗人使用“我”字的频率要高得多。

sentences.en: And, again, they're focusing so heavily on self compared to non-suicidal.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们与非自杀倾向者相比，确实过度关注自我。

sentences.en: That's really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这真的很迷人。

sentences.en: Isn't that interesting?
sentences.zh: 这难道不有趣吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And what we found was that people who benefited the most from writing would change in their use of pronouns over the course of the three or four writing sessions.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，从写作中获益最多的人，在三到四次写作过程中，他们对代词的使用会发生变化。

sentences.en: So one time they might use I words at high rates.
sentences.zh: 有时他们可能会高频率地使用“我”字。

sentences.en: And other times they're using other pronouns.
sentences.zh: 而另一些时候，他们会使用其他代词。

sentences.en: He, she, they, we.
sentences.zh: 他、她、他们、我们。

sentences.en: And then back to I and then others.
sentences.zh: 然后再回到“我”，接着又是其他代词。

sentences.en: And what they're doing is they're changing their perspective.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的是在转换视角。

sentences.en: And I think this therapist do this themselves when a client comes in and you ask them, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 我想治疗师在面对来访者询问“发生了什么”时，自己也会这样做。

sentences.en: Well, my marriage is a problem.
sentences.zh: “嗯，我的婚姻出了问题。”

sentences.en: And then they'll say, well, I feel this.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会说，“嗯，我感觉到了这个。”

sentences.en: I feel this.
sentences.zh: “我感觉到了这个。”

sentences.en: I feel this.
sentences.zh: “我感觉到了这个。”

sentences.en: I feel this.
sentences.zh: “我感觉到了这个。”

sentences.en: I feel this.
sentences.zh: “我感觉到了这个。”

sentences.en: And the therapist at some point will say, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 治疗师在某个时刻会说：“是，是，是。”

sentences.en: What about the other person?
sentences.zh: “那另一个人呢？”

sentences.en: What's going on with the other person?
sentences.zh: “另一个人那边发生了什么？”

sentences.en: Or if the person comes in, problems with my marriage, yeah, you know, my spouse does this.
sentences.zh: 或者如果来访者说“我的婚姻有问题，你知道，我配偶做了这个”。

sentences.en: They do this.
sentences.zh: “他们做了这个。”

sentences.en: They do this.
sentences.zh: “他们做了这个。”

sentences.en: And Sarah will say, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 治疗师会说：“是，是，是。”

sentences.en: But you, how do you feel?
sentences.zh: “但你呢，你感觉如何？”

sentences.en: Tell me about yourself.
sentences.zh: “跟我说说你自己吧。”

sentences.en: In other words, the therapist is naturally doing what people who benefit from writing do.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，治疗师自然而然地在做那些从写作中获益的人所做的事情。

sentences.en: They're able to go back and forth between self and others.
sentences.zh: 他们能够在自我和他者之间来回转换。

sentences.en: So changing perspective is helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以转换视角是有帮助的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And people who write the same way all three or four days hardly ever benefit.
sentences.zh: 而那些在三四天里写作方式一成不变的人，几乎从未从中获益。

sentences.en: And in fact, writing about the same story in the same way is really the same as rumination.
sentences.zh: 事实上，以同样的方式反复书写同一个故事，其实和反刍思维没什么两样。

sentences.en: It's almost a marker that writing is not beneficial.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是一个标志，说明写作没有起到作用。

sentences.en: And if you find that you tell the same story over and over again, you're not getting any traction.
sentences.zh: 如果你发现自己一遍又一遍地讲述同一个故事，那你并没有取得任何进展。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I was just going to ask another word-based question.
sentences.zh: 我正想问另一个关于词汇的问题。

sentences.en: You have talked about the difference between content words and style words.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了内容词和风格词之间的区别。

sentences.en: How are they different?
sentences.zh: 它们有什么不同？

sentences.en: What do we learn about analyzing those words?
sentences.zh: 通过分析这些词，我们能学到什么？

sentences.en: It's funny.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: That was what I think the biggest breakthrough I had with the language work.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是我在语言研究方面取得的最大突破。

sentences.en: When I started doing this, it was just at the creation of the internet.
sentences.zh: 我刚开始做这项研究时，正值互联网诞生之初。

sentences.en: This was about 1995, 96.
sentences.zh: 那大约是1995年或96年。

sentences.en: And there was this new invention called America Online.
sentences.zh: 当时出现了一个叫“美国在线”（AOL）的新发明。

sentences.en: And I suspect, Kim, you know about America Online.
sentences.zh: 我猜，Kim，你应该知道美国在线。

sentences.en: And I'm guessing many people out there in podcast land won't know it.
sentences.zh: 但我估计播客界的许多听众可能不知道它。

sentences.en: AOL.
sentences.zh: AOL。

sentences.en: AOL was this incredible breakthrough.
sentences.zh: AOL是一个了不起的突破。

sentences.en: You got a disk you put on your computer.
sentences.zh: 你拿到一张光盘，把它放进电脑里。

sentences.en: And if you had a modem, it allowed you to connect to the internet.
sentences.zh: 如果你有调制解调器，它就能让你连接到互联网。

sentences.en: And what was fascinating was AOL had these chat groups.
sentences.zh: 最迷人的是，AOL有聊天群组。

sentences.en: And you could be in these chat groups with people from all over the world.
sentences.zh: 你可以和来自世界各地的人在这些聊天群组里交流。

sentences.en: And for somebody like me, it was unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 对于像我这样的人来说，这简直不可思议。

sentences.en: Because you could download chats.
sentences.zh: 因为你可以下载聊天记录。

sentences.en: And what I would do is, at night, you know, we'd put the kids to bed.
sentences.zh: 我通常会在晚上，你知道，把孩子们哄睡着之后。

sentences.en: And then I'd go into my study.
sentences.zh: 然后我会走进书房。

sentences.en: And I would just go to chat groups.
sentences.zh: 直接进入聊天群组。

sentences.en: And I'd just download.
sentences.zh: 然后就开始下载。

sentences.en: And sometimes I'd go to chat groups that were predominantly women.
sentences.zh: 有时我会去女性占主导的聊天群组。

sentences.en: And others that were predominantly men and so forth.
sentences.zh: 有时去男性占主导的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I started looking at the differences at the beginning between men and women and how they use language.
sentences.zh: 起初，我开始观察男女在使用语言方面的差异。

sentences.en: And I had all of these theories that many people probably would share with that I had.
sentences.zh: 我当时有很多理论，很多人可能也会有同样的看法。

sentences.en: That I just assumed women would use we words at a higher rate than men.
sentences.zh: 我理所当然地认为女性使用“我们”字的频率会比男性高。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: There was no difference.
sentences.zh: 根本没有区别。

sentences.en: Well, at least men will use I words a lot more than women because they're much more narcissistic.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少男性会比女性更多地使用“我”字，因为他们更自恋。

sentences.en: Actually, women consistently use I words more.
sentences.zh: 实际上，女性使用“我”字的频率始终更高。

sentences.en: I was thinking, what the hell?
sentences.zh: 我当时心想，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And it must be a fluke.
sentences.zh: 这一定是巧合。

sentences.en: So, I tried it with other data sets.
sentences.zh: 于是，我尝试了其他数据集。

sentences.en: I kept finding it over and over again.
sentences.zh: 结果我一次又一次地发现同样的情况。

sentences.en: And what about cognitive words?
sentences.zh: 那认知词呢？

sentences.en: Well, men, you know, I would assume they use them more.
sentences.zh: 嗯，男性，你知道，我本以为他们会用得更多。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Women use cognitive words at much higher rates than do men.
sentences.zh: 女性使用认知词的频率比男性高得多。

sentences.en: Articles and prepositions.
sentences.zh: 冠词和介词呢？

sentences.en: Who knew?
sentences.zh: 谁能想到呢？

sentences.en: I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全没料到。

sentences.en: But men consistently use those more than women.
sentences.zh: 但男性使用这些词的频率始终高于女性。

sentences.en: And the only thing that I, oh, what about emotion words?
sentences.zh: 我唯一能想到的，哦，那情绪词呢？

sentences.en: Well, obviously, women use emotion words more.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然，女性会更多地使用情绪词。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: There's virtually no difference.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有任何区别。

sentences.en: The only difference were social words, references to other people.
sentences.zh: 唯一的区别在于社交词，即对他人的指代。

sentences.en: You know, friends, man, woman, child, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 你知道，朋友、男人、女人、孩子等等。

sentences.en: Women use social words at a much higher rate.
sentences.zh: 女性使用社交词的频率要高得多。

sentences.en: And that's the only one I got right.
sentences.zh: 而那是我唯一猜对的一个。

sentences.en: And I should tell you, when I've given tests to people all over the world and asked them
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，当我给世界各地的人做测试，问他们

sentences.en: who uses these different types of words, more men or women, everybody makes the same mistakes that I did.
sentences.zh: 谁会更多地使用这些不同类型的词，是男性还是女性时，每个人都犯了和我一样的错误。

sentences.en: Although nowadays, people are getting a little bit more sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 虽然现在人们已经变得稍微精明了一些。

sentences.en: But what's happening is the words that I had discovered are called function words.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我发现的这些词被称为功能词。

sentences.en: And these are words that don't have a fixed meaning.
sentences.zh: 这些词没有固定的含义。

sentences.en: So she means one thing in one context, but in another context, it's referring to another woman.
sentences.zh: 所以“她”在一个语境中指代一件事，但在另一个语境中，它可能指代另一个女性。

sentences.en: The versus a, the refers to something that you and I both know what it is.
sentences.zh: “定冠词”与“不定冠词”，定冠词指的是你我都知道是什么的东西。

sentences.en: When I talk about the table, somehow we've been referenced in our conversation before.
sentences.zh: 当我谈到“那张桌子”时，说明我们在之前的谈话中提到过它。

sentences.en: If not, we say a table, my table, that table, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 如果没有，我们会说“一张桌子”、“我的桌子”、“那张桌子”等等。

sentences.en: And these are all, these words are interesting because they're processing the brain differently and they're heavily, heavily psychological.
sentences.zh: 这些词很有意思，因为大脑处理它们的方式不同，而且它们具有非常深厚的心理学意义。

sentences.en: They're related to, as I suggested, depression.
sentences.zh: 正如我所建议的，它们与抑郁症有关。

sentences.en: They're related to telling the truth versus lying.
sentences.zh: 它们与说真话还是撒谎有关。

sentences.en: They're related to relative status.
sentences.zh: 它们与相对地位有关。

sentences.en: They're related to, you can get a sense of how long the two people have known one another.
sentences.zh: 它们与你能感知到两个人认识多久有关。

sentences.en: It tells us about their personality and much, much more.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们关于他们的个性以及更多更多信息。

sentences.en: So this was where I started to become so excited about how language could be used to understand individuals, but also couples, but also groups.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我开始对如何利用语言来理解个人、夫妻以及群体感到兴奋的地方。

sentences.en: And then I started to become interested in entire societies.
sentences.zh: 后来我开始对整个社会产生兴趣。

sentences.en: And nowadays with days with social media, we can start to track how a culture is shifting.
sentences.zh: 如今有了社交媒体，我们可以开始追踪文化是如何转变的。

sentences.en: So for example, with COVID, this is not going to come as any shock to anybody, but COVID turned our culture upside down.
sentences.zh: 例如，关于新冠疫情，这对任何人来说都不足为奇，但疫情确实颠覆了我们的文化。

sentences.en: And in some ways, it, in possibly permanent ways, certainly put us on a different cultural track.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，它可能产生了永久性的影响，当然也让我们走上了一条不同的文化轨道。

sentences.en: And we can see this through the analysis of Twitter or Reddit or other social media data sets
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过分析Twitter、Reddit或其他社交媒体数据集来观察到这一点，

sentences.en: that when an entire culture is anxious, the entire culture starts using I words at higher rates.
sentences.zh: 当整个文化感到焦虑时，整个文化开始以更高的频率使用“我”字。

sentences.en: They start using anxiety words at higher rates.
sentences.zh: 他们开始以更高的频率使用焦虑词汇。

sentences.en: One other thing that I think people will be interested in working with something like Reddit, we're
sentences.zh: 还有一件事，我想人们会对使用像Reddit这样的平台感兴趣，我们

sentences.en: able to download hundreds of thousands of Reddit posts, or we were, we could easily do it up until about a year ago, but we can still do it in other ways.
sentences.zh: 能够下载成千上万的Reddit帖子，或者说我们曾经可以，直到大约一年前我们都能轻松做到，但我们仍然可以通过其他方式做到。

sentences.en: Now, working with one of my students, Sarasaraj, what we started to do was to look at how do people behave when they are going through a breakup.
sentences.zh: 现在，我和我的学生Sarasaraj合作，我们开始研究人们在经历分手时会有什么行为。

sentences.en: And, you know, the ways that we study relationships in psychology historically has been, you know, find people who've had a breakup and give them questionnaires.
sentences.zh: 你知道，心理学历史上研究关系的方式通常是，找到经历过分手的人，给他们发问卷。

sentences.en: Tell me what it was like.
sentences.zh: “告诉我那是什么感觉。”

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 拜托。

sentences.en: This is a questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 这只是问卷调查。

sentences.en: Then people are constructing stories.
sentences.zh: 人们是在构建故事。

sentences.en: What's happening when they're going through a breakup?
sentences.zh: 他们在经历分手时到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, if you're lucky doing a big study, you know, a few people in your group will have a breakup and you can study them a little bit.
sentences.zh: 如果你在做一项大型研究时很幸运，你知道，你小组里会有几个人经历分手，你可以稍微研究一下他们。

sentences.en: You give them questionnaires.
sentences.zh: 你给他们发问卷。

sentences.en: But I don't find that very compelling research.
sentences.zh: 但我认为那不是很有说服力的研究。

sentences.en: I want to capture a large group of people going through a breakup and I want to track them every day of their lives from before to after.

sentences.en: So with social media, I can't do every day of their lives, but I can go to, there's a, one

sentences.en: Reddit is, it's anonymous.

sentences.en: But what we would do is if a person had posted at least a month before somewhere on Reddit and

sentences.en: And our, our, our admissions were, were a little bit more stringent than that.

sentences.en: We ended up getting about six to 8,000 people.

sentences.en: And then what we do is we go and look at all of their posts up to a year before the breakup and to one year after the breakup.

sentences.en: afters, meaning we are capturing their lives and their interactions with people that they're not even telling that they're having a breakup.
